problem:
Find the Laplace transform $L{{f}^{″}(t)}$ for $s>0,$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ ${f}^{′}(0)=3,$ $f(0)=-1,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{3-s}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is continuous and ${f}^{″}$ piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$

feedback.problem:
Find the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ for $s>3$ given that the function $f(t)$ is continuous over $[0,\infty ),$ $f(0)=5,$ and

$$
L{f(t)}=\frac{5s-6}{{s}^{2}-3s},\,s>3.
$$

Assume that ${f}^{′}$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose $F(s)=L{f(t)}$ where $f(t)$ is a continuous function of exponential order $a$ on $[0,\infty ).$ If ${f}^{′}(t)$ is piecewise continuous on $[0,\infty ),$ then

$$
L{{f}^{′}(t)}=sL{f(t)}-f(0).
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the Laplace transform of ${f}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{f}^{′}(t)} & =sL{f(t)}-f(0) \\  & =s\cdot \frac{5s-6}{{s}^{2}-3s}-5 \\  & =\frac{5{s}^{2}-6s}{{s}^{2}-3s}-5 \\  & =\frac{9s}{{s}^{2}-3s} \\  & =\frac{9s}{s(s-3)} \\  & =\frac{9}{s-3}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>3.$
